ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening for Politically Exposed Persons (PEP), OFAC sanctions, UN sanctions, and domestic AEAT/Registro Mercantil lists

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish language with mandatory use of Latin alphabet; company names must comply with Spanish orthography and naming conventions
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Protected words such as 'Estado', 'Rey', 'Real', 'Banco', 'Caja', 'Sociedad', 'Asociación' without prior approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name is rejected, file administrative appeal within 1 month to the Registro Mercantil Central or competent court; possible judicial review

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for most commercial activities including port-related services; Spain accepts virtual or registered offices for SL entities
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (standard risk for non-regulated industries); unannounced inspections rare unless AML or tax audit triggers

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Companies Act, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital, principally Articles 4, 19-23, 28-30, 58-63, 210-242, and 252-258; Commercial Registry Regulations, Royal Decree 1784/1996; Entrepreneurs Act 14/2013 for electronic processing through the CIRCE system.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, following name clearance by the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central). The notarial deed is executed before a Spanish notary public.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), accompanied by the certified negative certificate of company name, articles of association, evidence of share-capital contribution, beneficial-ownership information, and filing application for registration with the Provincial Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An SL may be incorporated with minimum capital of EUR 1. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000; on liquidation, shareholders may be jointly liable for the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. There is no statutory escrow requirement, but monetary contributions must be evidenced to the notary by a bank certificate or may be accepted under the statutory founder-liability alternative. Higher capital is commercially advisable for port licensing and credit requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and ratifies the subscription and full payment of its quota capital by the founding shareholder in accordance with the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office is adopted at [full Spanish address], with authority granted to update the address within the same municipality where legally permitted; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, if applicable, directors are appointed in accordance with the articles and accepted by signature; (4) [name] is appointed authorised signatory for banking, tax, registry, employment, port-authority and licensing matters; and (5) management shall complete all post-incorporation registrations and maintain statutory books.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Clear and Reserve the Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), Madrid, through its electronic name-certificate portal or through a Spanish notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names and obtain the negative certificate of company name. The certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed and may be reserved for the statutory period applicable to incorporation. Ensure the proposed name includes the legal form designation Sociedad Limitada or S.L.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if an agent files
Foreign-founder corporate documents, apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or request correction of the filing. If the certificate expires, obtain a new certificate before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles, Beneficial Ownership and Capital Evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public coordinating the incorporation file; tax and identification processing through the State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles covering name, object, registered office, capital, quotas, governance structure, transfer restrictions and financial year. Define the corporate object narrowly enough for licensing while covering ancillary logistics activities. Obtain a temporary tax identification number (NIF), identify beneficial owners, and arrange a Spanish bank certificate for monetary contributions unless the statutory founder declaration is used.
required_dossiers: Founder's passport or national identity document
Foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents and apostilled power of attorney, if applicable
Bank certificate of capital deposit or founder contribution declaration
Proposed director acceptance and declaration of non-disqualification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies requested by the notary, replace defective legalization or translation, correct the corporate object, or provide supplementary capital evidence before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public with territorial competence for the execution of the deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder or duly empowered representative signs the public deed. The notary verifies identity, capacity, powers, name certificate, articles, capital subscription and beneficial ownership. Foreign documents must satisfy apostille or legalization requirements and be accompanied by an official Spanish translation unless the notary accepts another legally valid form.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate certificates and legalized translations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve notarial observations before signing. If the deed is refused, obtain written grounds, amend the deed or supporting documents, and request a fresh execution appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and Register for Tax Purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT), through its electronic office or designated tax office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 for the provisional NIF and census registration. After Commercial Registry registration, submit the registered deed and obtain the definitive NIF. Register for VAT and intra-Community transactions where applicable, select the appropriate economic activities, and establish electronic notification access.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate for definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent activity codes, address data or identification details and resubmit Form 036. Respond to an AEAT verification request with the deed and ownership evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Deed with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered-office province, generally through the notary's electronic filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authorized electronic copy of the deed, articles, name certificate, tax identification documentation and beneficial-ownership declaration. Pay the applicable registry and publication charges, which are tariff-based and variable rather than a single national state fee. Obtain the registration entry and certified registry extract.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIF and tax filing evidence
Registry filing form and fee payment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a qualification notice, cure each defect within the applicable period and refile. A negative qualification may be appealed to the Directorate-General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith or challenged before the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Incorporation Governance and Employer Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry, AEAT, General Treasury of Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social), and the competent labor authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the definitive NIF, legalize corporate books electronically, record the first board or sole-director resolutions, register the company as an employer before hiring, and enroll employees and directors where required. Establish accounting, beneficial-owner, AML, data-protection and occupational-risk systems before operations commence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected Social Security or book-legalization filings, submit missing documents, and avoid hiring or commencing regulated operations until the relevant registration is effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The relevant Port Authority (Autoridad Portuaria) under the governing port's Board of Directors, supervised by Puertos del Estado; the relevant autonomous-community and municipal authorities also exercise environmental, industrial, planning and activity-control powers.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: License to provide the port service of cargo handling (Licencia de prestación del servicio portuario de manipulación de mercancías), under the Consolidated Text of the Law on State Ports and the Merchant Marine, Royal Legislative Decree 2/2011, principally Articles 108-115. A concession or authorization for occupation of port public-domain land and infrastructure is separately required where the terminal occupies or operates on port estate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental authority of the relevant Spanish autonomous community, with the Ministry for Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge acting as competent authority for projects reserved to the State.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening under Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment. A new or materially expanded bulk terminal, port infrastructure project, dredging operation or project within a protected area may require a full ordinary environmental impact assessment; other modifications may require simplified assessment or may be exempt only after documented screening. Operation may also require an environmental authorization or municipal environmental activity approval.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Obtain the applicable discharge authorization for wastewater and stormwater, comply with the limits and monitoring conditions imposed by the basin or coastal authority, apply Best Available Techniques where applicable, control bulk-material dust and VOC emissions through enclosure, extraction, water suppression and monitoring, and manage hazardous and non-hazardous waste under Law 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils. Exact numerical limits depend on cargo, receiving environment, permit and autonomous-community rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before commissioning, obtain municipal opening or activity authorization and, where required, an environmental activity license; secure fire-safety compliance under Royal Decree 513/2017 and the applicable building and industrial fire regulations; complete structural, geotechnical, crane, conveyor, silo, pressure-equipment and electrical inspections; implement occupational-risk prevention under Law 31/1995; comply with port emergency and security plans, dangerous-goods rules, ATEX requirements where explosive atmospheres may arise, and workplace coordination obligations. Port-specific access, security and emergency approval must be obtained from the relevant Port Authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores and the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Customs matters are administered through the AEAT Department of Customs and Special Taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) from the AEAT. The incorporation process normally involves obtaining a provisional NIF using Form 036, presenting the incorporation deed or equivalent formation documentation, identification of the administrator or authorized representative, and evidence of the registered office. Following execution of the deed, registration with the Mercantile Registry, and completion of the corporate documentation, the company must request confirmation or conversion to a definitive NIF through Form 036 within the applicable statutory period. The company must also register its business activities, tax domicile, VAT status, withholding obligations, and intra-Community operator status where relevant. A foreign corporate shareholder generally requires a Spanish NIF for tax and administrative purposes; its legal representative may require a Spanish NIE or other accepted identification. A non-resident entity conducting taxable activities in Spain generally applies for a Spanish NIF through Form 036 and must appoint or identify an authorized representative where required. Registration in the Register of Intra-Community Operators (ROI) and validation in the VIES system are required before carrying out qualifying intra-Community supplies or acquisitions using an intra-Community VAT number. An EORI number is required for customs operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal taxpayer and has no general United States-style check-the-box election. It cannot generally elect to be fiscally transparent merely by filing an administrative classification form. Relevant elections and regimes may include tax consolidation for qualifying Spanish tax groups, the special regime for small enterprises where statutory conditions are met, the cash-basis VAT regime (Régimen Especial del Criterio de Caja), the monthly VAT refund regime, the immediate supply of information regime (SII), and qualifying special regimes under Spanish and European tax law. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch provisions implement applicable ATAD rules and may deny deductions, impose inclusion, or otherwise neutralize hybrid arrangements; they do not create a general entity-classification election. Territorial special regimes, including the Canary Islands indirect tax system, are separate from mainland Spanish VAT and require separate factual qualification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), Spain's VAT system. Mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands apply Spanish VAT; the Canary Islands apply the separate Impuesto General Indirecto Canario (IGIC), and Ceuta and Melilla are outside the territorial scope of Spanish VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold exempts a person carrying on an economic activity in Spain from VAT registration. A taxable person must register in the census before commencing taxable activities, making supplies, acquiring goods intra-Community, importing goods, or undertaking other transactions giving rise to VAT obligations. The Spanish VAT system does not provide a broad United Kingdom-style annual registration threshold. The taxpayer must file the appropriate census registration, generally Form 036, and obtain the relevant NIF-VAT status. Certain supplies may be exempt, outside scope, or subject to special place-of-supply rules, but those classifications do not establish a general VAT registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a single universal real-time pre-clearance system for all commercial invoices. Businesses must issue and preserve VAT-compliant invoices containing the legally required supplier, customer, date, description, taxable base, rate, VAT amount, and invoice-identification data. The Immediate Supply of Information (SII) system requires qualifying taxpayers, including taxpayers in the monthly VAT refund regime, large enterprises exceeding the statutory turnover threshold, and VAT groups, to transmit specified invoice-register data electronically to the AEAT, generally within the prescribed short filing periods. The Law on the Creation and Growth of Companies provides for progressive B2B electronic invoicing obligations, subject to implementing regulations and effective-date conditions. The Spanish anti-fraud invoicing framework, including the Veri*Factu requirements, is being implemented through technical and transitional rules and requires compliant invoicing software, traceability, integrity, and anti-manipulation controls when applicable. Separate regional systems, including TicketBAI in the Basque Country, may apply based on tax residence or activity. Electronic customs declarations and EORI-based customs messaging apply to exports and imports, but customs clearance is not a substitute for VAT invoice compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands to destinations outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT under the Spanish VAT Law, provided the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU and the exporter can substantiate the transaction with reliable customs and transport evidence. The exporter must retain the commercial invoice, export declaration and customs exit confirmation, transport documentation, proof of delivery or destination where relevant, and records linking the goods to the export transaction. Intra-Community supplies may qualify for exemption with the right to deduct where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier retains required documentary and reporting evidence. Services supplied to business customers established outside Spain may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the applicable place-of-supply rule rather than technically being zero-rated exports. Services directly connected with qualifying exports or international transport may qualify for specific exemptions only where statutory conditions are met. Port-terminal stevedoring must be analyzed by reference to the customer, cargo movement, contractual chain, and whether the service is directly connected with an exempt export or international transport operation; the fact that a service is performed at a Spanish port does not by itself establish zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, VAT treatment, and transaction terms
Customs export declaration submitted through the Spanish customs electronic system, normally containing the relevant export procedure and commodity information
EORI number of the exporting entity and, where applicable, the customs representation authorization
Export accompanying document or equivalent customs reference and electronic confirmation that the goods have exited the customs territory of the European Union
Bill of lading, sea waybill, cargo manifest, terminal movement record, or equivalent transport document
Packing list, weight records, cargo identification, and port loading or gate-out evidence
Transport contract, freight documentation, and proof of delivery or arrival outside the European Union where relevant
Evidence linking the customs declaration, invoice, cargo, and payment to the same export transaction
Customer VAT identification evidence for qualifying intra-Community supplies, together with transport evidence and required EC Sales List reporting

Bank payment records or other commercial settlement evidence where required for audit support; Spain does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a universal condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general foreign-exchange rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days as a universal condition for VAT zero-rating. Payment and banking records may nevertheless be examined as corroborative evidence, and sector-specific, contractual, customs, anti-money-laundering, or foreign-investment rules may impose separate requirements. If an export exemption is unsupported or incorrectly claimed, the AEAT may assess the unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties, and may deny or reverse related input-VAT deductions. Fraudulent, simulated, or deliberately concealed transactions can trigger severe tax penalties under the General Tax Law, including penalties based on the amount improperly obtained or not paid, and may result in criminal tax exposure where statutory thresholds and intent requirements are met. Customs violations may generate separate customs debt, administrative penalties, seizure or forfeiture consequences, and post-clearance reassessments. Refunds obtained through false documentation may be recovered with interest and penalties. Taxpayers must retain accounting, invoice, customs, transport, and supporting commercial records for the applicable statutory limitation and record-retention periods, commonly four years for ordinary Spanish tax assessment purposes, subject to extensions, interruptions, longer periods for assets or tax attributes, and other applicable legal requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating as the national central bank and the Spanish component of the European System of Central Banks (ESCB). Ultimate monetary and foreign-exchange policy authority resides with the European Central Bank (ECB) because Spain is a full Eurozone member. The Banco de España exercises supervisory and financial-stability powers under the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) and executes Balance of Payments (BoP) statistical monitoring under Circular 4/2012.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both capital and current account across all Spanish payment channels. Spain imposes no general foreign-exchange licensing regime, no exchange rate bands, and no capital-repatriation approval system. The free movement of capital and payments is constitutionally and treaty-grade protected under Articles 63–66 TFEU and also facilitated by the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2). Profit and dividend remittance by a Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted for EU/EEA residents; for third-country shareholders, remittance is equally unrestricted in currency terms, but a 19% withholding tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes) is generally applied unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty. Intra-EU dividends are exempt from Spanish dividend withholding where the 5% participation threshold of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) is satisfied. Foreign direct investment into a port stevedoring entity is not screened or conditioned on exchange approval, although large investments may trigger statistical filing. All capital movements with non-residents greater than or equal to EUR 50,000 per transaction, or EUR 50,000 cumulative in the same calendar year, require the mandatory electronic declaration to the Banco de España (Form T1 for transactions with non-residents). These declarations are for statistics and not for authorisation, and therefore present no convertibility hurdle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender, no obligatory conversion timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds. A Spanish stevedoring and port-terminal SL may retain its full export and cross-border service proceeds in EUR or in any freely convertible foreign currency. Export settlement proceeds received from non-resident charterers, shipowners, or cargo consignees are held at the Spanish bank without time limit. Nonetheless, the statutory reporting rule under Banco de España Circular 4/2012 requires that any export-related collection from a non-resident exceeding EUR 50,000 be included in the monthly T1 BoP return, submitted within fifteen business days after the month-end. For USD- or third-currency-denominated export proceeds, the exporter may hold the foreign exchange balance or convert into euro at the prevailing ECB reference rate without any requirement to liquidate a designated percentage. Failure to file the T1 report can produce administrative fines but does not affect the legality of holding the underlying FX proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (corporate checking, payroll, tax disbursements) and temporary capital-subscription account for the SL's initial paid-in capital
Operational Account (full SEPA, documentary credit, and local concessions cash-management)
Operational Account and digital-only remote onboarding option
Operational Account (direct corporate/global desk for non-resident shareholders)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH as a supplementary foreign-exchange and collection rail; LOW as a primary or sole treasury account. A Spanish SL must maintain a Spanish IBAN EUR account to satisfy SEPA compensation, SSI tax refunds, payroll mandatory social-security settlement, and port-authority concession payments. Non-resident digital EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Monei, Qonto) legally passport their EEA licences into Spain under PSD2, and can be integrated for USD/GBP collections and better FX spreads. However, they do not provide documentary credit (LC issuance), corporate credit cards backed by an onshore credit line, Spanish port-authority gateway collection, or full access to Banco de España T1 reporting; these services require a domestic Tier-1 bank. A dual-rail structure is legally viable: primary domestic Spanish account for all clearing and compliance, plus an offshore EMI sub-ledger for FX optimisation, provided every cross-border movement above EUR 50,000 is included in the Spanish T1 BoP declaration. No regulatory veto exists on holding funds with an EEA-licensed EMI, but the SL's treasury policy should keep the EMI exposure below 10% of average liquidity to mitigate counterparty risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the statutory default for directors and all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) under Spanish AML Law 10/2010 (Ley de Prevención de Blanqueo de Capitales). Each director and any shareholder holding 25% or more of the capital must appear in person at the branch or before a Spanish notary to verify their identity; for a remote corporate client the senior compliance officer requires an in-person or notarised risk interview. Royal Decree-Law 5/2023 now permits fully remote notarisation (firma notarial remota) for directors residing outside Spain, allowing onboarding without physical travel, provided the bank has SEPBLAC-accredited video identification. In practice, Tier-1 banks accept the following hybrid: (i) Spanish-resident director appears at the branch; (ii) non-resident director executes a public power of attorney (poder/escritura de apoderamiento) in favour of a Spanish agent or legal counsel; the power-of-attorney holder attends the KYC interview on the director's behalf. All banks require the first UBO compliance interview to cover the business model, counterparty profile, anticipated transaction volumes, and source of funds for the paid-in capital, especially for a port-terminal entity with active cash-intensive stevedoring operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a corporate shareholder registered in a jurisdiction with a nominal corporate tax rate below 40% or in a shell/holding structure that raises automatic 'tax transparency' red flags under Article 4.3 of Law 10/2010 and SEPBLAC guidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership-chain organisational chart traced to natural persons; audited or review financial statements of each intermediate entity; certificate of good standing from the registry of the foreign jurisdiction; Spanish corporate registration (Registro Mercantil) plus escrito de ampliación; UBO passport copies; Notarial deed (escritura de constitución) showing economic substance; employment contracts and physical rental lease in the shareholder's jurisdiction; transfer-pricing file (documentación maestra y de valoración) evidencing arm's-length intercompany flows; source-of-funds sworn declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Port/maritime activity involving bulk cargo (coal, ores, grain, fertilisers) posing dual-use goods and sanctions-signal screening; banking watch-lists map the ISIC 5224 code to high-risk CCAFT sectors and may reject the account due to unknown end-beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid operational licence granted by Puertos del Estado and the relevant Autoridad Portuaria concession contract; ISIC 5224 registry entry; customs DUA/DAE declarations for at least one recent cargo cycle; charter-party agreements listing verified vessel names and IMO numbers; International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) certificate; counterparty bank SWIFT BIC and KYC passport issued by the receiving bank; signed declaration confirming no transaction in embargoed/high-risk jurisdictions; compliance manual excerpt describing the physical cargo-control and screening procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection from a non-resident shareholder in a LATAM country (e.g., Peru, Brazil, Mexico) with diversified FX-origin and remittance flows, creating unusual-activity flags and potential cross-border anti-money-laundering exposure for the receiving Spanish bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised board resolution and capital-increase deed registered at the Registro Mercantil; bank certificate from the source bank confirming the remitter is the same UBO; SWIFT MT103 MT199 proof with purpose code 'Direct Investment'; sworn statement of source of funds signed by the shareholder; personal/professional wealth background statement; audited financial statements of the sending entity; prior-year BoP declaration if previous transfers were made; written commitment from the SL that the injected funds remain at least 12 months and are used for capital equipment and terminal infrastructure, not for tax arbitrage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High daily cash volumes associated with stevedoring gangs and temporary dock-winch subcontractors can generate a currency-structuring suspicion or trigger the state's anti-cash threshold of EUR 1,000 for business payments (Law 7/2012).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank payroll order to each worker via SEPA instant credit, with social-security settlement in TARGET2; signed policy declaring a zero-cash treasury cap and a prohibition of invoice payment in cash for amounts exceeding EUR 1,000; payroll register (recibos) reconciled monthly; contracts with temporary staffing suppliers; cashier's log showing POS or 24-hour ATM disbursement does not exceed de minimis; completed Banco de España S.1/T.1 declarations proving traceability of every cash-in and cash-out operation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: A compliant inbound capital injection from a foreign shareholder (e.g., a Latin American parent or non-EU investor) to the Spanish SL is routed exclusively through the SWIFT MT103 payment message to the SL's Spanish IBAN. The mandatory wire narrative must include the purpose code 'Inversión Directa' (Direct Investment) under the Banco de España BoP classification, with a descriptive reference 'Capital Increase Deed No. XXX' and full legal owner details. The receiving Spanish bank requires, as documentary verification of the underlying economic operation, the public deed of capital increase (escritura de ampliación de capital) authorised by a Spanish notary, evidence of entry in the Registro Mercantil, and a bank certificate certifying the deposit prior to the increase. For an SL with minimum capital of EUR 1 (full paid-in capital is due at constitution), large injections are treated as capital increases and are free from any Spanish foreign-investment authorisation; no prior declaration is necessary under EU screening Regulation (EU) 2019/452 unless the injection originates from a subsidised non-EU operator. All amounts over EUR 50,000 are declared by the bank to the Banco de España on Form T1 within 15 business days. If the injection is transferred in a foreign currency, it is converted at the ECB reference rate, and any conversion cost is borne by the investor. In the event of a transfer of shares rather than cash, the non-resident purchaser must advise the Banco de España of the securities transaction for statistical purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements from the Spanish SL to non-resident counterparties use the following clearing hierarchy: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct account-to-account commercial disbursements (bunker suppliers, international subagents, vessel owners) with attached BoP code 'Pago a no residente' and full invoice references; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits) issued by the SL's Spanish bank governed by UCP 600 for high-value charter or port infrastructure purchases, with MT700/MT707/MT799 messages handling issuance, amendments, and negotiation; (iii) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SEPA Inst) and SEPA CT for EU resident suppliers and intra-EEA partner disbursements; (iv) TARGET2 for high-value euro payments requiring deterministic finality on the same day, reserved for port-authority concession fees and customs guarantees; and (v) in the rare USD-denominated disbursement channel, a correspondent clearing via JPMorgan Chase or BNY Mellon through the SWIFT network, or CHIPS, with the Spanish bank initiating an MT202 COV where the beneficiary is the SL's own branch account. Shipping-port authorities in Spain (e.g., Autoridad Portuaria de Valencia) provide a dedicated clearing interface for cargo-handling fees and concession tariffs, typically by direct debit (SEPA DD) and RTGS; the SL treasury should implement API-based reconciliation against these rails to avoid late-payment surcharges.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD foreign exchange forwards (Outright Forwards) with tenors up to 24 months allowing the SL to fix the euro cost of USD-denominated stevedoring and bunker disbursements.

FX swaps (Spot-Forward Swaps) combining a spot EUR/USD transaction with an offsetting forward leg, used to manage short-term liquidity mismatches between the USD collection rail (port charges invoiced in dollars) and the EUR operating ledger.

Cross-currency swaps (CIRS) aligned with long-term USD/EUR cash-flow mismatches arising from port concession financing or long-dated charter liabilities, documented under the ISDA Master Agreement and mirrored with the Spanish clearing bank.

Plain-vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP options (call/put on euro) for selectively protecting the SL's export-tariff exposure while preserving upside when the nominal value of the underlying exceeds EUR 500,000 per quarter.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin American currencies (e.g., USD/PEN, USD/BRL, USD/MXN) where the port terminal invoices or trade counterflows are generated respectively in Peruvian sol, Brazilian real, or Mexican peso; Spanish licensed banks offer these subject to the bank's internal credit limit, an ISDA-backed confirmation confirming a genuine commercial underlying, and hedging alignment with monetisable receivables denominated in the referenced currency; no regulatory prohibition exists as long as the operation is within the SL's ordinary treasury policy and reported under the bank's standard derivative self-assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within six months from fiscal year-end; deposit within one month from approval. Calendar-year SL: approval by 30 June, deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) for new filings; directors jointly liable; administrative fine from EUR 1,500 to EUR 300,000 under the Consolidated Spanish Companies Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 25 October of the year following the tax period for calendar-year taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late surcharge 5%–20% plus arrears interest; minimum EUR 200; inaccurate or omitted turnover triggers penalty of 50%–150% of the omitted amount per General Tax Law 58/2003.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 January of the following tax year for calendar-year taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine EUR 150; unfiled or erroneous returns expose the company to full VAT assessment plus 50%–150% misdeclaration penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of transactions with third parties (Modelo 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 28/29 February following the tax year; obligatory when aggregate transactions with a counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06 per year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 150 per omitted counterparty or 2% of invoicing volume, minimum EUR 1,500; false returns may incur criminal penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) annual update (Registro de Titulares Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (integrated with the annual accounts deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual accounts deposit; calendar-year entities must update the UBO statement by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry block on subsequent corporate acts; non-compliance penalties up to EUR 60,000 under Law 10/2010 on money laundering and terrorist financing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for the SL if at a fiscal year-end it exceeds, for two consecutive years, at least two of: balance-sheet total over EUR 2,850,000; net turnover over EUR 5,700,000; average staff over 50. Any steady exposure above these thresholds triggers the statutory audit duty under the Spanish Companies Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Local GAAP (Plan General Contable, Real Decreto 1514/2007); IFRS-EU only for listed or consolidated filings; annual accounts include balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in equity, cash flow statement and notes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must file the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner with the annual accounts deposit; any notarized share transfer requires an updated UBO declaration at the next deposit, and the directors must retain documentary evidence for ten years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Journal and Inventory/Annual Accounts Books (Libro Diario and Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 150–600 (USD 160–640) for a standard registered office and compliance agent; higher in prime Madrid/Barcelona locations.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 4,500–15,000 (USD 4,900–16,200) for a medium-size port terminal operator, dependent on consolidations, inventories and permanent establishment risk.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) during the first two tax periods, provided the taxable base is positive and all legal requirements under Article 29.3 of Ley 27/2014 are met. General regime: no sector-specific reduction for port stevedoring; however, participation exemption (95%) under Article 21 LIS applies to qualifying dividends and capital gains.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no time limit; offset capped at 70% of positive taxable base per year, subject to a mandatory EUR 1,000,000 minimum offset, per Article 26 LIS)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically through the Sede Electrónica de la Agencia Tributaria (AEAT)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days of the six-month post-year-end period (for calendar-year taxpayers, by 1 October of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, and fiscal year of the Spanish SL
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ownership is not declared in this box; the SL’s Spanish NIF and corporate name are entered as registered in the Mercantile Registry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish registered office address and port terminal location
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the physical Spanish address of the stevedoring terminal; no foreign parent address should be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross annual turnover from stevedoring, cargo handling, port services, and ancillary logistics income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue from the Spanish port operations must be fully recorded under Spanish tax law, regardless of invoicing to foreign parent or related entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resultado contable (accounting P&L) before tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SL’s statutory financial statements; no non-resident adjustments or off-book transactions are permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base imponible after statutory tax adjustments (depreciation, impairment, corrections, arm’s length adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply standard Spanish adjustments. If the parent non-resident holds controlled transactions, any transfer pricing adjustments under Article 18 LIS must be incorporated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 012 (Applicable tax type and integrated fee)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax charge at the applicable statutory rate (25% or 15% for new entities)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the rate as per law; non-resident shareholders do not influence rate selection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly progress payments (Modelo 202) and any withheld Spanish tax on income paid to the entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct prepayments actually made. Dividend withholding to non-resident shareholders is not part of this declaration; it is reported using separate forms (Modelo 216/296).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax due or refundable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount is the residual after prepayments and credits. Subsequent distribution to non-resident shareholders is subject to independent withholding tax and treaty procedures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge (recargo) for Modelo 200: 5% of the amount owed if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% within 6 months; 15% within 12 months; 20% thereafter. Interest de demora at 3.75% annual. If no tax is owed, fixed fine EUR 200. Incorrect/incomplete forms face penalty of 15% of the amount not declared, with minimum fine EUR 300 (Arts. 25, 27, 198 LGT).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (Article 25.1 of the Non-Resident Income Tax Code, Real Decreto Legislativo 5/2004)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced withholding tax under a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must submit a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) to the Spanish paying entity before the dividend payment. The paying entity retains the TRC and applies the treaty rate. If the TRC is not available, the default 19% must be withheld; the shareholder may subsequently claim a refund by filing Modelo 210 with the AEAT, attaching the original TRC, dividend documentation, and proof of withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 19%; reduced under DTAs; 0% under EU Interest/Royalty Directive for related EU entities (25% ownership held for at least 2 years). Royalties: statutory 19% (subject to base erosion provisions); treaty rates typically 0–10%; 0% under EU Interest/Royalty Directive for qualifying related entities.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 annual net turnover (cifra anual de negocios) triggers mandatory preparation and filing of Transfer Pricing Documentation (Local File and Master File) under Article 18 LIS and Articles 14–15 of Royal Decree 634/2015. Below this threshold, the taxpayer must retain sufficient evidence of arm’s length pricing but is not required to prepare full documentation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) – Método del Precio Libre Comparado
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) / Margen Neto Transaccional
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) but enforces Economic Substance and anti-abuse principles under Article 15 LIS (Business Purpose Doctrine) and Article 34 of the Spanish General Tax Code (simulation and sham transactions). A bulk port stevedoring SL is presumed compliant if it maintains the statutory stevedoring license, operates physical terminal infrastructure, employs local staff, contracts actual dock labor, and conducts transactional activity in Spain. The existence of such substantive operations protects against treaty-shopping challenges and denial of DTA benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional understatement of cargo-handling fees, systematic cash payments not recorded, or false invoices from subcontractors; failure to declare turnover from stevedoring operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code (Ley Orgánica 10/1995): if the amount evaded exceeds EUR 120,000, imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and fine of the 6-fold evaded amount. Tax-Administration penalty under Article 191 LGT: 50% to 150% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate or tolerate tax fraud are jointly and severally liable under Article 43.1.b LGT for the corporate tax debt and penalties. Criminal liability may extend to the director if they knowingly signed false accounts (Art. 310 bis CP); civil restitution is mandatory; travel bans and disqualification from serving as director of any Spanish company can be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating an SL for the sole purpose of holding a port stevedoring license while all actual loading/unloading, billing, and risk management operations are performed by a non-resident parent or associated entity outside Spain, with no physical office, dock personnel, or operating assets in Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will disregard the entity under Article 16 LIS (economic substance look-through) and re-attribute income to the actual owner; corporate income tax reassessed with 50%–150% penalty surcharge; denial of DTA benefits and loss of treaty protections. Administrative fines up to EUR 30,000 for simulation under Article 16 LGT may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face joint liability for the full tax underpayment if they act as purely nominal managers with no real oversight. In egregious cases, directors may be charged with criminal tax fraud or corporate crime under Article 310 bis CP, leading to fines, restitution orders, and prohibition on obtaining port licenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large cash payments from unidentified cargo brokers or using shell suppliers to launder illicit proceeds, in violation of the Spanish AML Law (Ley 10/2010, as amended). A port stevedoring terminal is a cash-intensive business and operates as a financial gate for trade proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine under Articles 57–58 Ley 10/2010: up to EUR 30 million or five times the subject value for serious infringements. Criminal money laundering under Articles 301–302 CP carries imprisonment of 1 to 6 years; if committed as part of organized activity (e.g., a cargo fraud consortium), sentences can be higher.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are aware of laundering and fail to enforce controls are criminally liable as accomplices or principals. Civil liability for the full amounts laundered; travel bans and personal seizure of assets are standard preventive measures during investigation. Directors may also face mandatory removal from administrative roles in any licensed port entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating intra-group tariffs for stevedoring services (e.g., setting service fees below arm's length to shift profit to a low-tax parent or related logistics entity) without proper benchmarking documentation; failing to file documentation when turnover exceeds EUR 10,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish tax authorities will apply Article 18 LIS and impose a transfer pricing adjustment, increasing the taxable base. A penalty of 15% on the adjusted amount (Article 21.1) applies, plus late-interest; the illegal transfer pricing of above EUR 250,000 per transaction may be considered serious, leading to 150% penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign TP documentation knowing it contains false figures face criminal tax fraud liability if the adjustment exceeds EUR 120,000. They are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under Article 42.2.a LGT, and travel/witness requirements during the audit can be imposed. In cross-border cases, directors can be extradited under EU Council Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA for serious fraud.
